summary: unreservedDispatches audits every review-log row since the parent's created_at against only the parent's reservations. Review dispatches a delegated child reserved and settled in its own ledger are flagged as BUDGET_CHECK_SKIPPED, so the parent's close stops with exit 3 / status=incomplete on every delegated run whose segment includes Step 9 or 11.
evidence: Scratch test: start cap 80M -> check (delegate) -> handoff 7-11.5 -> verify-handoff -> child check --next dispatch:specialist -> review-log --start --reservation <child id> (exit 0) -> --finish (settled) -> return -> reconcile (child=complete). Then the parent's close printed 'CLOSE 3 ... (role=review step=9 ... spend=unknown) (BUDGET_CHECK_SKIPPED)' and 'STOP: reason=budget_check_skipped dispatches=1'.

summary: The per-branch marker stays until close, and activeLedger treats any capped, unclosed ledger as active, including a stopped one. After a /ship cap stop or an abandoned run, every gstack-review-log --start on that branch (standalone /review and other review skills) is refused. While a capped /ship runs, a /review in another session is also refused because it has no reservation.
evidence: Scratch test: start --token-cap 20M --reading 0; check --step 1 --next 2 --reading 19000000 -> exit 3; then a plain 'gstack-review-log --start review' -> exit 1 '... run ... stopped at Step 1: budget_exhausted ... (BUDGET_CAP_REACHED)'.

summary: Under meter=estimate, readMeter always returns call=null, and the segment rule treats null as over the threshold. A run with --delegate never (hosts without children, which the estimate meter is for) always stops with context_threshold at Step 7, whatever the cap and usage.
evidence: start --token-cap 200M --meter estimate --delegate never; check --step 6 --next 7 -> exit 3 'STOP: reason=context_threshold call=unknown threshold=150000 next=7 (--delegate never)' with used=2250000.

summary: resume --meter capy without --reading opens the new epoch at baseline 0 (tokensOpt(o,'reading') ?? 0) and does not demand a reading. The next reading of the Capy root counter then counts the thread's entire prior spend as this run's usage.
evidence: start --meter estimate (cap 200M); resume --meter capy (no --reading) -> exit 0 'EPOCH: 2 meter=capy'; check --reading 50000000 -> 'BUDGET: used=50000000'.

summary: On the Claude meter, resume rebinds the session only when the meter kind changes. 'resume --session <new id>' in a fresh session, which the context_threshold RECOVER line tells the user to do, keeps metering the old session, so the new session's spend is never counted against the cap. Ledgers rebuilt with --rebuild-from-record bind no sessions at all.
evidence: pickMeter returns 'claude' for --session; `if (meter !== l.meter.contract.meter) {...bindClaude...} else readMeter(l, o, false);` ignores --session. rebuildLedger builds meter without sessions/config_dir, so readClaudeUsage sums nothing.

summary: newEpoch carries 0 when the closing epoch is meter=estimate, so settled estimate_used is dropped from used after a meter change. tally only adds estimate_used while the current meter is estimate.
evidence: `const metered = l.meter.contract.meter === 'estimate' ? 0 : ...; l.carried_used += metered;` while tally uses l.estimate_used only when the current meter is estimate.

summary: The per-branch marker is removed only by `close`. A run that stops (the skill says to print STOP and end) or is abandoned leaves it behind, and from then on every `gstack-review-log --start` on that branch is refused, including a later uncapped /ship and a standalone /review. An uncapped `start` returns early in cmdStart (lib/ship-budget-cli.ts:165) without clearing the stale marker.
evidence: Scratch test: `start --record r1 --token-cap 100 --reading 0` -> exit 3 STOP; then `start --record r2` (no cap) -> exit 0 'BUDGET: unmetered'; then `gstack-review-log --start review` -> exit 1 'gstack-review-log: ... (run ship-... stopped at Step 0.9: budget_exhausted) ... (BUDGET_CAP_REACHED)'. admitReviewStart throws when l.stopped; only cmdClose unlinks l.marker; budget-handoff.md.tmpl's verdict=stop says to end status=incomplete with no close.

summary: cmdResume only calls bindClaude when the meter kind changes, so `resume --session <new id>` on a claude-metered run ignores the new session. The context_threshold RECOVER line says to resume 'in a fresh session', and that session's usage is never metered, so the cap stops working.
evidence: Scratch test: start with --session A (1000 tokens); `resume --record r --session B` -> exit 0, sessions unchanged; append 900000 tokens to B's journal; `check --step 2 --next 3` -> 'BUDGET: used=0 ... verdict=continue'. Code: `if (meter !== l.meter.contract.meter) { const sessions = meter === 'claude' ? bindClaude(o, ctx.env) : undefined; ... } else readMeter(l, o, false);`
